::: {.cite-bar .domain-war-powers}
[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Pub. L. 92-403]{.cite} [86 Stat. 619]{.cite} [1 U.S.C. 112b]{.cite}
:::

Requires the Secretary of State to send Congress the text of international agreements other than treaties. It was a response to secret executive agreements, including basing and security commitments, discovered in the late 1960s.

## Key provisions

- Transmission of executive agreements to Congress, originally within 60 days of entry into force.
- Classified agreements go to the foreign relations committees under an injunction of secrecy.
- 2022 amendments: monthly reporting, public posting of texts, a statement of the legal authority for each agreement, and coverage of certain non-binding instruments.

## Why it matters

It is the main transparency check on executive agreements, which far outnumber treaties. It belongs with the [War Powers Resolution](wpr-1973.qmd) and the [National Emergencies Act](nea-1976.qmd) as part of the 1970s effort to restore congressional visibility into foreign commitments.

## Current status

In force, substantially rewritten by section 5947 of the FY2023 National Defense Authorization Act (Pub. L. 117-263).
